global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; ordering is inferred from limited corroborating signals, and citation evidence is sparse for papers only days old. It is not a popularity ranking.

sections.title: Conductivity of electrolyte solutions: Self-consistent Debye-Hückel-Onsager theory
sections.abstract: The authors develop a self-consistent Debye–Hückel–Onsager framework with smeared ionic charge distributions to derive conductivity contributions across aqueous and non-aqueous electrolytes.
sections.claimed_result: The paper derives analytic mean-field, correlation, and electrophoretic conductivity terms and reports agreement with published conductivity data across several valences, concentrations, and solvents.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; analytic classical density-functional/Ornstein–Zernike framework compared with published aqueous and non-aqueous conductivity measurements
sections.unique_caveat: Ion- and solvent-specific charge-smearing lengths are fitted to data; predictive transfer beyond the tested solvents and input parameter uncertainty remain to be established.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate score 3.219, driven by 4 current Semantic Scholar citations (0 influential; about 1.17 current citations/day after age normalization); this is the strongest citation component in the supplied pool. PCCP publication/DOI is corroborating context, not a score component.

sections.title: Structure and relaxation of long-lived odd-parity modes in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
sections.abstract: The authors calculate how odd-parity Fermi-surface distortions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids relax, finding that thermal dressing and large-angle scattering alter the leading-logarithmic prediction.
sections.claimed_result: Including nonlogarithmic collision-integral terms, the authors find partial thermal dressing and benchmark the constant-interaction relaxation spectrum against exact diagonalization, resolving a discrepancy with the leading-log estimate.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; low-temperature collision-integral calculation, benchmarked against exact diagonalization for constant interactions
sections.unique_caveat: The exact-diagonalization agreement is reported for a bounded parameter range (m²T/T_F ≲ 0.4) and a constant-interaction benchmark; the general result assumes regular isotropic potentials.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate score 1.886 combines 1 current Semantic Scholar citation (0 influential; about 0.33 current citations/day after age normalization) and 2 cross-lists. The paired thermopower paper provides a concrete adjacent transport result, not independent confirmation.

sections.title: Thermopower overshoot from collinear scattering in two-dimensional Fermi liquids
sections.abstract: The author predicts that thermal dressing of Fermi-surface distortions causes a wave-vector-dependent thermopower overshoot in two-dimensional Fermi liquids, including under realistic disorder.
sections.claimed_result: The kinetic calculation predicts an overshoot above the hydrodynamic thermopower followed by a fall toward the ballistic value, with low-temperature excess decreasing logarithmically rather than linearly.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; kinetic-equation/collision-matrix calculation for two-dimensional Fermi liquids with disorder
sections.unique_caveat: The overshoot is a theoretical prediction, not a reported observation; the authors propose a high-mobility thermocouple as a possible test.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate score 1.886 combines 1 current Semantic Scholar citation (0 influential; about 0.33 current citations/day after age normalization) and 2 cross-lists. Its close connection to the preceding Fermi-liquid mode paper makes the two a coherent theoretical cluster, not independent confirmation.

sections.title: Regularizing gravity in the presence of matter fields
sections.abstract: The authors derive conditions for regular spherical black-hole and cosmological geometries to remain regular when scalar, electromagnetic, or radiation matter fields are present.
sections.claimed_result: Within a class of second-order spherical gravitational theories whose vacuum solutions have bounded curvature, they find that matter coupling does not generically remove the possibility of regular solutions.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; analysis of spherical black-hole and cosmological solutions with scalar fields, electromagnetic fields, and radiation fluids
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusions are conditional on spherical symmetry, second-order field equations, and the selected class of regular-vacuum theories; they do not establish regularity in generic spacetimes.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate score 1.636 combines 1 current Semantic Scholar citation (0 influential; about 0.29 current citations/day after age normalization) and 1 cross-list into hep-ph. Its stated conditions address both black-hole and cosmological geometries.

sections.title: Entropy production from crossing a quantum separatrix
sections.abstract: The authors show that slow passage through a dense quantum avoided-crossing spectrum approaches a universal separatrix and produces diagonal entropy after realistic averaging over parameter ramps.
sections.claimed_result: In the quasi-continuous semiclassical limit, the paper derives a universal one-parameter family of separatrices and an entropy-production formula, with numerical examples retaining the behavior in finite systems.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; semiclassical analysis with numerical examples for finite systems
sections.unique_caveat: The entropy result relies on averaging over small variations in parameter time dependence and on the extreme semiclassical/dense-spectrum regime; finite-size effects remain relevant.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate score 1.636 combines 1 current Semantic Scholar citation (0 influential; about 0.25 current citations/day after age normalization) and 1 cross-list. The universal semiclassical result is a concrete cross-disciplinary theory signal.

sections.title: Disentangling Lengthscales in Disordered Fracture
sections.abstract: Using a two-dimensional random-fuse model with Weibull disorder, the authors distinguish the crack-tip screening length from the regularizing length in the quasibrittle size-effect law.
sections.claimed_result: Their simulations show distinct disorder dependences for the two length scales and suggest that the size-effect length may relate to percolation of pre-failure microfractures.
sections.evidence_type: computational; two-dimensional random-fuse simulations with Weibull-distributed disorder and a coarse-grained load-redistribution model
sections.unique_caveat: This is an idealized two-dimensional model; the proposed microfracture-percolation interpretation is a candidate mechanism, not an experimental validation in heterogeneous materials.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate score 1.000 from 4 cross-lists is the largest cross-list component among selected entries. The work connects disordered statistical physics with applied fracture mechanics.

sections.title: Bayesian Quantum Thermometry of Ultracold Gases with Non-Equilibrium Single-Atom Probes
sections.abstract: The authors experimentally use non-equilibrium spin-exchange dynamics of single-atom probes for Bayesian ultracold-gas thermometry and find adaptive measurements need 2.5 times fewer repetitions than an unoptimized protocol for the prescribed precision.
sections.claimed_result: Adaptive expected-information-gain measurement reduces the average number of measurements required to reach a target precision by a factor of 2.5 versus the unoptimized protocol.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; spin-based single-atom probes immersed in an ultracold atomic bath, with Bayesian inference from measured spin populations
sections.unique_caveat: Inference depends on probe spin dynamics and measurement settings; the paper identifies intersections of temperature-dependent population trajectories as a source of ambiguity.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate score 0.750 from 3 cross-lists; an openly deposited dataset (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24390998) adds a reproducibility signal outside the score.

sections.title: Molecular structure breaks universality in screening behavior of electrolyte solutions
sections.abstract: Using machine-learned classical density-functional theory across increasingly detailed electrolyte models, the authors find solvent and ion structure change screening modes and exponents, opposing a universal law across these models.
sections.claimed_result: The calculations find solvent attraction can add a monotonic decay mode, solvent polarity can produce re-entrant behavior, and ionic structure can change screening-length exponents.
sections.evidence_type: computational; machine-learned classical density-functional calculations over a hierarchy of electrolyte models
sections.unique_caveat: The result is model-based rather than a new measurement; mapping the model hierarchy onto specific concentrated solutions requires experimental comparison.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate score 0.750 from 3 cross-lists. The paper addresses the disputed universality of concentrated-electrolyte screening with a systematic model hierarchy.

sections.title: 60-cm-long In-vacuum Zerodur Optical Cavity for Optical Lattice Atom Interferometry
sections.abstract: The authors describe and characterize a 60-cm in-vacuum Zerodur cavity designed to support long-coherence optical-lattice atom interferometry and localized gravity measurements.
sections.claimed_result: They measure mirror vibration below 5 nm/√Hz across 2 Hz–100 kHz and a 15 MHz resonance drift over 47 hours, which they report can be stabilized with an integrated piezo.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; optical-cavity prototype with measured mirror vibration and resonance drift
sections.unique_caveat: Millimeter wavepacket separation and one-minute measurement duration are design goals; the abstract reports cavity characterization rather than a completed atom-interferometry demonstration.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate score 0.750 from 3 cross-lists; measured vibration/drift characterization gives a concrete instrumentation result within the tied-score group.

sections.title: Topological phases protected by half-chiral symmetry
sections.abstract: The authors formulate topological protection by half-chiral symmetry, with real-space invariants and boundary modes, and construct a two-dimensional model with a protected zero-energy corner state.
sections.claimed_result: For a half-chiral Kekulé honeycomb model, the authors show higher-order topology protects a single zero-energy mode at one corner.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; symmetry and topological-invariant construction illustrated with a two-dimensional lattice Hamiltonian
sections.unique_caveat: The result is a theoretical construction; the symmetry condition must be realized and distinguished from ordinary chiral symmetry in a material platform.
sections.ranking_evidence: Candidate score 0.750 from 3 cross-lists. Its proposed symmetry framework and boundary-state construction are the concrete result used to break the tie within the score group.
